This won't work in the case of a B40, where the card itself is the PCIe device, which also needs to include the FRU.  Also doesn't work in the case where there's more than one NSM device on a single device (NVL32).

We can enable PCIe properties for GPUs separately. This patch is limited to PCIe properties support for CX devices. If a platform has more than one CX device, we already append Device Instance Id (retrieved from device via MCTP VDM command) to the DBus Object Path name and hence multiple devices would appear as PCIe Devices in redfish.

> multiple devices would appear as PCIe Devices in redfish.

Right, this is the bug.  In the case of things like Alon8, with multiple Cx8s on the same board, exposing them as separate PCIe devices might not be correct.
Fixed. Now we would have a DBus Object Path per ConnectX device (instead of PCIe device) and we populate PCIe interface properties of each of the ConnectX.
@ed@tanous.net not sure why exposing each CX as a PCIe device is incorrect.
Done
Because we have one "device" that hosts multiple CX8s.
In terms of the existing OpenBMC D-Bus interfaces, each CX8 is a PCIeDevice and the board itself is a PCIeSwitch, isn't it?

> each CX8 is a PCIeDevice

In terms of Redfish interfaces, I expect that each CX8 would be in the same API?  If not, lets document where that is that one physical device could be representing two devices.

"The `PCIeDevice` schema describes the properties of a PCIe device that is attached to a system. It also describes the location, such as a slot, socket, or bay, where a unit can be installed, by populating a resource instance with an absent state if a unit is not present."

If we're noting the "slot" it's plugged into, it would be nonsensical to have two devices in one slot?
Since each ConnectX has a unique PCIe address on the Host CPU, each ConnectX can be modeled separately as a PCIe device.
Can you test this on Alon8?

I have tried to follow the pattern that already exists for GpuDevice. Here PcieDevice is class representing a device, just like GpuDevice, and all device sensor (PCIeInterface class is one of the sensor) are member data of the device class.
